metadata.notes:
Notes:
-- Seamless transition between Discs 2 and 3.
-- Dragon Parade during Drums.
-- Supplication tease in Unlce John's Band.
-- Those aren't drop-outs and cuts, it's a gate (Google it).
-- Check out Phil's bass line in Corrina.

reviews.reviewbody: This is the best sbd out there of this show.There is one more out there thats pretty good but you can hear the crowd but its not like an Audience recording its like the audience got mixed into the sbd or somthing I think it just got toned out but its a real good job.But some dont like the audience in there show even if it sounds realy good.Im just letting ya all know.But I give this sbd 5 for sound and still a 4 for the show

Great sounding SBD and quite well-played show. Sloppy start of the set one and only after Mexicali band finally fired up. After this it was a great pleasure to listen to the music and of course there were some interesting surprises during second set.

Corrina is a blast with powerful bass lines and nice guitar solos. Before this warm and inspired version of UJB ended with nice Supplication tease and of course don't forget about the highlight of the concert what is notorious for being one of the biggest letdowns of the era: instead of Cosmic Charlie which seemed imminent Jerry turns to Wharf Rat. Being a fan of this song I won't grumble. 

Turn on Your Lovelight and Rain were great pieces to finish the show.

I was sitting right next to my friend Mr. Miller for this show. Right over that right side back entrance over the floor. The Cosmic tease hands down the cruelest thing Jerry ever did. Never will I forget giving Charlie high fives and hugs then seeing his face as it became Wharf Rat. " I'm outta here" is all he could say.
I sang a little while and then flew on.

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

Well played show here, with a fantastic Cosmic Charlie Tease>Wharf Rat.

@TerrapinLanding - There was nothing excellent about that Cosmic Charlie tease. It wrecked the whole night and I still think about it to this day. That shit was coldhearted, and believe me when I say that no one in that arena was glad they saw a Cosmic Charlie tease.

JIm Blackwood and John Bradford interviewed him on March 5 before the show.
The audio circulates and is transcribed as well.
https://www.angelfire.com/fl/goodbear/healy-interview.html

A "best of" musically, as well as extended portions of the interview, was broadcast on 91.3 FM KXCI Tucson on Dead Air,  March 7, 2021 - hosted by Jim Blackwood and Jamie Waddell.  https://spinitron.com/KXCI/pl/12762487/Dead-Air

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

After trudging through the very lackluster Phoenix, AZ, run that came before it, this show was refreshing. Much better energy in both sets I and II, with Jerry in fine form for a High Time, Scarlet>Fire, and good take on an up-tempo Dark Star. The Drums>Space goes some interesting places, but it is not as good as 3/5 (26 minutes of pure headiness), which is the standout thus far among the first shows of 1994 that I have listened to. Nice Miracle towards the end too, which almost launches into a Truckin' jam. Vince plays well throughout. I like his '94 selection of keys and vocals. SOTM goes out with a bang!

reviews.reviewbody: This is an amazing show.  From start to finish this show smokes.  Great setlist, great playing all around.  I can say this is one the first shows that made me understand and appreciate the Grateful Dead.
reviews.reviewtitle: Great Show!!!  So glad to get the SBD.

reviews.reviewbody:
Hello,

As you can probably tell I have never written a "review" for anything in my life--excepting computer products.

That being said, I was (and AM) a "deadhead" to the core of my soul!  This show, in particular, explains why.

As a Suburban Chicagoan, the Rosemont Horizon (now the "All-State Amphitheater--but of course) has housed many a great band and LOTS of memories.  My first concert, Billy Joel (in 1980) was there (and AWESOME!)  So was my first Dead experience, in 1987.

I got tix for the three-night Horizon run, 3/16-3/18.  While all three where notable in some fashion, this one was "the ONE"--Jerry's voice and playing as fluid as ever, Billy and Mickey chugging along like 10,000 locomotives, Bobby non-annoying, Phil up LOUD in the mix dropping bombs, and Vince proving his worth as a post-Hornsby keyboardist.  He's not Brent, but then who IS?  He held his own.

I will not lie--this was when I was 24 and, for the last night, I imbibed in some fine local-brewed L.  I'm glad I did, kinda, because this set the tone for the night.

I had good seats where I wanted them--just off floor in the rear of the arena so I would be placed for perfect stereo...although little did I know that the MeyerSound PA stuff being used then would "generate" perfect stereo just about anywhere you sat throughout the arena via very accurate FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) real-time sound analysis, active room-sampling and EQ, and many other tricks that Healy and Pearson had up their sleeves back then.  They were about 20 years ahead of the "live-sound" curve then!  Still, I was low enough to catch floor-coupled bass and great imaging and high enough to get a good view of the lights and not be in the way of the HF driver arrays.

"Stranger" rang out after the Boys took to the stage after a quick tune-up, Vince roaring along on B3.  Wow, Bobby sure sounds good!  I always like a good "Stranger!"  Bobby sings with emotion and perfection; Jerry's wah-picking very fluid and on-key.  Granted, I could deal without the MIDI guitar/cheezy 80's synth in the chorus, but hey...  Vocal harmonies are all on, very good.  I hear that Jer sounds awesome despite two hard shows before.  I am excited!  Bobby sings, "You know its gonna get stranger, so let's get on with the show!" and the crowd roars its approval.  Stranger indeed!  Jer's noodling in the Stranger jam is spot-on.

"Deal" starts, to my delight, with Jerry picking out the notes with precision.  Vocals are SOOOO good!  Vince in on some piano--very Hornsby-like, low in the mix.  Jerry flubs the first three notes of his first-verse solo--the rest are precision itself, like pieces of sparkling stained-glass!  Wow, I'm thinking, he must REALLY know this song!!  WHOOPS, a vocal mistake where I thought the organ solo went!  So they sing the first verse again and, well, what?  Jer's trying to steer the band to the closing jam, Vince is feeling cheated out of his shining moment...hmm.  A moment of confusion as Jerry looks over at Phil and shrugs, smiling.  Still, Jer's fretboard runs in the close solo are SO good--and Vince is jamming chords along with him on his grand.  He's making up for the lost B3 solo VERY well.  Phil is shaking his way into my very soul.  It is continuous JAM from 3:25 onto the 8:21 end, except for a reprise of the "Deal" chorus at about 7:40.

I start to feel some the anxiety of onrushing psychedelics.  Oh man, what a mistake I think, this show is TOO GOOD for altered perception!!!

El Paso is next, and I dunno WHAT to think.  I mean, I LIKE the song, but at the time am all sour on Bobby songs.  When Bobby picks up an acoustic I get excited though.  Vocals are really good, Jer's "highlights" perfectly placed and played, vocal harmonies are so sweet!  OK, this version changed what I thought of El Paso!  Sweet ending with Bobby strumming, Jerry running, and such.  El Paso is a great song!

Starting to notice the floor and walls losing solidity, oh boy.  Feeling that anxiety that's the precursor for a HEAVY psychedelic experience...my God, that was FAST!  My hand cramps up--or does it?  Oh, what a great El Paso Jerry solo!  It's hard to notice though as the lights are starting to smear and every person is leaving trails in my vision...  Maybe I had too much too fast?  Little do I know it then, but I am experiencing my very first overwhelming panic attack, soon to be a fixture in my life.

"Brown-Eyed Women" is next...another song that I have only heard played to its potential on this night.  The climaxes of the song build to the chorus, the choruses to the bridge!  I can hear Jerry perfectly, his voice sounds acoustically STELLAR.  They must have done something, or not, to Jer's vocal equipment...it's that sweet and smooth.  TOTALLY not there for the previous two nights...at least it sure don't sound like it!  Sounds like perfect vocals run through a Nuemann 87 and a valve amp...my God, the WARMTH is astounding!!!  The band cranks this out like a perfectly-lubricated precision German-made 12-cylinder engine...everything meshes--harmonies, melodies, geometries, modalities, mini-solos, EVERYTHING!  The band sure was NOT dusty, and the liquor was clear and potent.

The L has hit me full-on.  I am starting to panic a bit more.  I reach for the Thorazine in my hipsack.  My friend there with me is like "NO!!!"  I put it back.

Masterpiece sounds after some tuning.  Bobby sounds SO good!  Better than Dylan Himself??  Maybe?  Vince is chording along, piano perfect, gotta change that cheesy synth sound!  Jer nails the first solo.

A small dimensional tear appears before my vision, in which I fancy I can see the Central Galactic Suns, as Jerry nails the solo as only he can, bending and wringing out every human emotion from his six steel strings.  The key change goes perfectly.  I am starting to experience a strange sense of synthesia now--every player has their own COLOR!!  Jerry is bright orange, Bobby yellow.  Bob and Jer NAIL the harmonies at the end of the song to loud cheers.

NOW I am starting to seriously lose it.  I regret ever taking ANY drug and pray to God, if He's indeed There, to make this stop.  I am, for some reason, praying the next song is a Jer tune, so I can chill out a bit at least!

Thus begins "Ramble On Rose."  Jerry plays the beginning perfectly with Vince playing honky-tonk piano.

As the first verse is sung, I experience the Dead as I never have experienced ANYTHING.  The Dead as Grand Design.  Everything in such perfect synchrony with everything else that it transcends music--hell, it transcends ALL EXPERIENCE!!  And, no, its not the acid.  LISTEN to it!!!  It's sheer perfection and grace.  The guitar solo is spot-on, with a lot of very welcome Jerry embellishments.  Oh my God, just when you think it cannot POSSIBLY go on it does, Jerry reaching for the heights, his music soaring like a magnificent flight of eagles on a desert thermal.  Never before has music done this to me!  My soul feels the freedom of total boundlessness...I have seen MANY Dead shows before this and always thought I "got it..."--but I never did.  Until now.  Just re-listening gives me chills!!!  Mickey and Billy are synched up like a gear on a chain.  As I hear it now, the guitar solo sounds just as good as it did that night.  It is very near note-perfect.  BY FAR the best RoR I have heard before or since.

The catharsis comes when Jer sings the "Just like momma and poppa..." line.  He sings it loudly, stridently, confidently.  He KNOWS he's "on" tonight!!  Sadly, I never hear him perform this well again.  Perfect.

Mentally, that RoR got me REALLY excited, but maybe too much so.  As "Music" starts I realize that I am in a bad place--my body looks like Michaelangelo as every muscle and tendon is standing out in sharp relief and PULLING at the same time.  This is pain like I have not known!  Jer's run at the beginning of TMNS makes me smile, but, oh God!!  I think that I should get a paramedic, decide to self-administer 60mg of Valium instead along with a friend's berry wine cooler (and I NEVER drink!)  My friends clearly SEE that there is something VERY wrong here, and try to talk me down a bit.  Only hurting.  So, although I remember TMNS as being a GREAT version and well-played that night, I am fighting for my life--at least so I think.  I remember the 3/4 part (or is it 6/8) being very "purposeful" and beautiful as fractal patterns drift over the floor crowd from the gobos.  Still, I never really connected with TMNS, and pray for a setbreak soon.

OK, 15 minutes into setbreak, but nowhere near OK.  The Valium has loosened my muscles but I need this trip to STOP!  Now!  And it has not.  Not by a long shot.  I grab for my hipsack and plunge the Thorazine syringe into my leg and wince at the pain as I push the plunger down.  5 minutes later I feel very sleepy and my trip is DEFINITELY over.

I remember a very awesome "Sunshine" second-set opener but drift off during the second verse.  I wake up in the back seat of a friend's van...at home...after the show.

Well, I guess that THIS is exactly why I am not a good reviewer!!  Yes, what I did was stupid.  Today I cannot even look back at that person as "me!"

Still, I had to share the pure and simple ALCHEMY of this show...it DID change my life and my attitude towards the Dead and live music in general.  It sets the bar to which I judge all others--perhaps unfairly, but it did.  I hope that you were able to groove on the vibe that I'm trying to send out about this show, and have had your OWN personal 3/18/1994!  This show (at least the first set) has yet to be surpassed.  Five stars with a cherry on top!!  THIS is the reason SBDs exist.

DoctorRon
October 12, 2009
show was hot & more than a couple of folks were freaked out at the early deal

U.S. Blues is most likely from an audience source-the sound quality is noticeably worse than the rest of the show. Lack luster that should have had a 2nd verse Dark Star tucked somewhere inside it. The first set (with the exception of Stranger and Deal) sounds hurried and rushed as if they could not wait to get off stage for a break. Shortest Brown-eyed women I have ever heard. This was not the way I would have liked this 3 night run to end, but alas, it was St.Patty's day the night before so perhaps the guys were pooped. Eh - win some lose some - 3 stars. 


~ Let the good times roll

I was pleasantly surprised by how well played this entire show was upon first listen. Perhaps not as much slam bang as the Brent days nor a mind bending set list but lots of intricate details that prove not only how far Vince has come since being fully on his own in the late spring 1992 but that everyone else is exploring new avenues within the structure too. Great 3 night run.

Fair show to end what was -- for me -- a better than expected sp94 Rosemont run. Not as good as the spring prior, to be sure, and this third night finale is the the weakest link, but overall it's still good. Plenty of lyrical mishaps, but the music is mostly well-played and enjoyable. Stranger opener is always a crowd-pleaser and of course the early set Deal must have surprised many. Here Comes Sunshine opens the second set to much applause, Saint is on-point and the two Jerry ballads (early Ship of Fools and late Wharf Rat) are very nice, again notwithstanding the lyrical issues. Otherwise, it's a forgettable three star show.
I sang a little while and then flew on.

reviews.reviewbody:
Thanks for adding this to the archive.
Box of Rain is an excellent version. 
The band seems really energized.

Four times the GD played Nassau on a March 28th, And they all were exceptional:

1985:  Truckin-Smokestack (w/M Kelley) opener
1990:  Easy To Love You, Loose Lucy, The Weight
1991:  Space-China Doll, Terrapin encore
1994:  Rain, That Would Be Something, Days Between

Mahalo to Hunter Seamons and Matthew Vernon for providing us with so many recordings!

reviews.reviewbody:
Not sure that's saying much but...

Nice long Scarlet>Fire, and the Playin' into the final Dark Star is really nice too. I used to have a tape of just that much, glad to get to hear the rest here.

(See my full review in SBD_miller)

As I look back and listen to the shows of this period it has become more and more clear that this show was a real blessing.  The Band was coming off months at home, and starting their main tour run.

Jerry is fresh and rested.  His leads and vocals are simply brilliant.  The band is tight as can be.  Phil and Bobby are in peak form.

The Drums and Space in all three shows of this stand are just INSANE good!

Highly recommended.  The best Jack-A-Roe of the 90's IMHO - bar none.

New Speedway Boogie (my fave GD song) was a beautiful surprise at this show.  It is, without doubt, the best version since the late 70's, no foolin'.

Enjoy!

What an *astounding* "Space" that is...

Perfectly timed for a DMT trip.....

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

Set 1:

We almost get a top-tier Picasso Moon, until the wheels come off the tracks. Deal in the #2 song slot like on 3/18. Great vocals from Vince. Dire Wolf with trumpet MIDI? Black-Throated Wind was not as good as it was in the Nassau run. Bird Song is dec. I'm still liking 3/30 as the best first set from this run.

Set 2:

This set delivers the goods. Listen from beginning to end. This would be great to pair with 3/30's set 1. VERY respectable China>Rider followed by a killer Box of Rain; Phil just nails it. He's Gone is a Jerry bust-out moment, but not super amazing. That Would Be Something only played 16 times. Drums>Space is worth the spin. 30 mins of headinesss, and one of the better performances thus far in '94, right up there with 3/5. Other One gets interesting. Sweet, sweet Brokedown to close it out.

reviews.reviewbody: It was a magical evening since the show the night before had to be cancelled. Jerry was very engaged and on point, nailing Terrapin. The Orlando Sheriff's Office had petitioned for new riot gear and been denied. Demonstrating how much it was needed, they were able to successfully restrain and breakup a vicious mob of drug fueled Deadheads who were on a rampant path of destruction threatening the safety of the band inside lol. Nothing quite like a Deadhead riot! The guys were in on the fun as seen and heard by the end of the show with I Fought the Law. Leaving the venue with daydreams in our head and pepper spray in our eyes and nose! I turned 21 that night. RIP Fred Jones

Cool! Over 20 years later a partial soundboard surfaces!

Yeah, good old Memorial Stadium. A chilly/chill June evening in 1994 Seattle. Good golly it was fun.

Jerry's playing his heart out. Huge Scarlet-Fire. Morning Dew (still missing in SBD) is a thundering set closer. Couldn't ask for much more than that out by the relay stacks in the damp dark and eerie!
the FOTM is really something else!

reviews.reviewbody:
22:41: Corrina (12:11)->Drumz (29:48)->The Last Time (7:00)->Days Between (14:07)->OMSN. 

Grossly overstated - in reviews in other streams - on the musical quality (or lack thereof) of this show. While I think '94 is probably the band's lowest point in their storied history, this show is not all that bad. Sure, it's no 6/18/74, but it's average '94 dead. Average '94 is obviously not average '74 dead, which is still great. I'm not as harsh on Garcia as njpg is, but I do agree that this show's highlights are definitely the new tunes: Easy Answers to close set one, Corrina into an excellent Drumz, and the always show-stopping Days Between, lyrical warts and all.

reviews.reviewbody:
This was the year I finally made the trip, finally after 14  years,to experience the Dead, California & the Great Northwest together. This tour was a perfect compliment to the spring tour and it was one of my most memorable touring adventure ever. Eugene was hollow ground for the Dead and the entire extended family and these three shows featured the best of that spirit with great music and full out hippie zaniness,camping & vending was allowed on site too.This was a day show and the sun was out and it was glorious,maybe even hot for Orgeon. Beautiful hippie women in their straw sun hats and  flowing summer dresses, flying marshmellows, a first  for me, melting quickly after contact creating stands of sticky goo along with the occasional flying tortillia. The vibe was quite festive but mellow.The band opened up with a solid Touch that was very well received. Walkin had us all feeling around for our shoes. A nice early  surprise with a joyous BEW that really set the groove. What a treat to hear El Paso in Oregon, you just had to think about Venata as I am sure many did. Actually the last one they played one here was 10/2/77 indoors, so it was a special moment. Shoe fits was good and then a deep and spacey Bird Song, that may have been one of the best in years. It is soaring with great vocals from Jerry and we all knew we were clearly there.We were about 30 ft on the floor on Phil's side, so were were staying put for a highly antiscipated second set,
Set II starts off with a slower paced but heartfelt Scarlet, folks were shooting off silly string in the front of the stage it was hilarious, which confidently expands into one of the longer tranistions with Jerry exploring and  delving deeper before arriving at the mounatin. Phil, Bob and Jerry really play it out and the end jam is the one of the  highlights. Samson just rocked the stadium and is a classic ripping version. WTGH is played with passion and the band continues to get stronger. After almost 45 mintues they pull out Playing, which is a suprise, a nice short textural jam sets up for one of the best UJB you will hear. Amazing   spot on vocals with clarity and joy, it is right on. Jerry's  solos again are outstanding. No long jam afterward, but hey we are already an hour plus into the set. Billy and Mickey continue to up the ante and  we plunge even deeper into space, they really shine on this night. Bob  Bravole does some cool soundscapes at the end. Space is good but nothing totally outragious, more like pyschedelic pinball which is  fun to listen to. It gradually intensify into an enormous Other One, the  transition and the intro by Phil and the band is ripping. They develop and explore this full out for five minutes, before Bob evens sings the first  verse, one of the best and longest of the 90's by far! Easily a perfect moment, I would also  suggest listening to the Cal Expo version too. A wonderful tranistion into a perfect reading of Whart Rat, Jerry is incredible and Vince really display his prominence with sweet harmonies and great playing. There is an audience patch during the last jam, I hope the master is perfect in the vault, and except for  some static in Touch this board is perfect. Good Lovin is icing on the cake, a joyous reading from Bob that is straight head with no silly rant on this one.We were all in nirvana. You get two minutes of cheering, which is wonderful, and then another gem. An epic and perfect reading of Knockin'. Beautiful vocals and harmonies adore this version and Jerry solo's are emotionally powerful and exquisite. One of the best encores I had ever witnessed. As the sun was setting that night,the band simply just blew us away. The Shakedown scene after the show, with the golden light of dusk reflecting on all our smiling faces, was beautiful and fun. I have to mention the food vendors. There were some of the best I had ever seen on Shakedown and those salmon burgers, I had them on all three nights, were incredible! I ate two or three after this show, no grilled cheese this night.We went to Cougar hot springs the next day and then onto Sequoia before going to Vegas, oh what a life we had back then.
reviews.reviewtitle: " He's come to take his children home"

reviews.reviewbody: I really feel bad for Vince Welnick. Kicked out of the Dead and not invited to play with the Other Ones (a band billed as "the surviving members of the Grateful Dead"), Vince is often made fun of as the keyboard player nobody likes. Some believe that his rejection by Deadheads and the band were big factors in his suicide. He must have felt bad when Horsby would sit in at shows and the crowd would go wild. People would rave about how Bruce gelled with Garcia and the guys just loved him. If it's any consolation Vince, I saw Hornsby open for Ratdog in 2006 and he sucked! People were screaming for Ratdog and it was a C- performance. I hate his solo stuff! He did kick your ass with the Dead though. Sorry man...you just didn't have what it took most nights. That is not true for this show!This is one of the very majestic nights the band played in the mid 90's. A truly inspired Bird Song, a Scarlet/Fire to remember with killer interplay, and one of the best Playing>Uncle John's Band>Other Ones you will find from the 90's. You had your moments Vince, but over all...sorry man you just didn't have the chops like Keith or Brent. The legend of Vince Welnick will find a spot in Grateful Dead history just above the black chicks who sung back up for the Jerry Garcia Band! Hahahaha sorry again dude!

Hey, don't be hatin' on Jackie and Gloria-
they were/are phenomenal, and were an integral part of the JGB at that time.  They also enjoyed the scene very much,as I remember from being at the stage for countless Warfield Jerry shows...

What a great trip from Yosemite it was to beautiful Eugene. Great scene. I remember a very intense pair of twins, if I remember correctly, jamming among the campers. They called themselves "Double Dose." They jammed hard.

It was dumb that I saved my money and didn't check in the other two nights, but this night was very good, especially the 2nd set and 1st set's Bird Song. 

You may want to patch Touch with an audience source as there are several points with static near the beginning (noting missing, but the static is awful). Thankfully, Wharf Rat and Good Lovin' are already patched

After the shows, I was glad to be in Roseburg, OR, for a while--David Grisman quarted jammed at the part there for free one day, and it was excellent!

Very long 2nd set, almost 2 hours!
1st not too shabby either. One of the better 1994 shows. There are two teases of note: before the 1st set there is a hint of I Want To Tell You (Beatles), and before So Many Roads, Jerry teases Deal. 
And, as always, thank you Charlie Miller.

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

Traffic was on the bill for these shows, so the Dead turned up ready to play. 

Set 1 Highlights: El Paso, Tom Thumb's Blues! Decent TMNS jam. 

Set 2 HIGHlights: Very cool Victim. Check out that into and outro jam into Eyes though. Box is great, but Saint of Circumstance might be the best I've heard in '94. Jerry nails the solo. Casually slips into a 23 minute Terrapin (that sadly has some timing issues; the outro jam also isn't as creative as other dates in '94). Nice Drums>Space>Wheel. Dew is Dew.

reviews.reviewbody: Definitely the best show of the 3... best cover to cover show I had seen in quite a while and Jerry showed up for the whole thing. By the time night fell and space trailed off into Stella, I forgot all about the Safeway down the street getting completely overrun by heads. Mountainview really was THE BEST place to see a show. ( The gold flaked black pyramids weren't bad either... but that's a whole other story!! )

This was the last worthy show I saw. .

The opening was stellar and it was steadily downhill till the end.

The best 3 days I spent anywhere!!! After a long and winding journey from Philadelphia to San Francisco couped up with my best pal in a small blue Horizon we found ourselves facing a sea of beauty, friendly faces and sparkling ambiance backed by the wandering licks of Jerry, Bobby and the boys. Thanks for the memories!!!

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

Set 1 HIGHlights: Big fun going on in the first set. I've heard better Eternitys but everything else is gold. 

Set 2 HIGHlights: Very respectable Help>Slip>Frank. Probably the best version of Shoe Fits I've heard thus far. First Smokestack Lightning of '94. DRUMS>SPACE IS A MUST-LISTEN FROM BEGINNING TO END. Wonderful Stella and Bobby songs on the outro.

reviews.reviewbody:
You couldn't ask for a higher quality sound with all 3 guitarists clearly laying down their lines and weaving together with keyboards and drums.  Bobby's playing is truly outstanding.
Highlights include a super Foolish Heart, a rare I Want to Tell You, an extended pre-drums space out of Playin' that will blow you away, a calypso-like Throwin' Stones after a perfect Wharf Rat and an extended Not fade Away to close.
Bonus:  the 2nd Beatles' cover, the harmonically sung and played Rain.
Definitely worth a listen and you can add in 1st set Shakedown and Maggie's Farm
reviews.reviewtitle: Great sound and two Beatles' covers

reviews.reviewbody:
Twenty years done come and gone my oh my!
I have a lot of personal memories from this show but I'll stick to the music. I will say that I saw Jesus at this show...those in the know will know what I'm talking about ;-) Hard to believe it's been twenty years! 
While this is a solid show for 94, the Playin>Drumz>Wharf Rat is way beyond the norm. In fact, this Playin is one of the very best of modern times. 
The opening Shakedown is very funky and showcases the absolutely PERFECT digital SBD. The middle of the first set is solid but uninspiring. Unfortunately this set has both Broken Arrow and Cheesy Answers...two of the worst songs in the Deads repertoir. Cheesy Answers has to be one of the worst first set closers, talk about leaving a bad taste in your mouth!
Second set is really just a build up and come down from the incredible peak during the Playin jam. The Foolish Heart is definately not among the best(check out 6-11 or 6-16-93). Saint is well played. I Want to Tell You is a rare treat but is really just an intro to the Playin, it's a trip hearing the final instrumental come unglued as they morph into the space vibe for Playin. Then the countdown into Playin. The lyric part is pretty standard but as the jam starts to develop it becomes clear that this is no ordinary version. I would call this the best Playin of modern times if it wasn't for 5-26-93 (as incredible as it may seem, the Playin from 5-26-93 actually ranks with the very best versions from 73-74, and thats saying something! Do yourself a favor and check it out sometime, it wont dissapoint) Back to this Playin-the jam is very visual, like a masterpiece painting. It starts off as a beautiful Hudson Valley School landscape painting, then slowly starts taking on a somewhat sinister Salvador Dali aspect with the trees starting to melt and strange otherworldly creatures wandering through the landscape. From there, it starts coming completely unglued and splatters of color splash across the canvas in Jackson Pollack fashion. Complete chaos is achieved as the intensity builds to an insane climax that has to be heard to be believed! Then we float into the ether as the jam resolves itself back into a landscape image, this time a beautiful sunset scene, WOW what a jam!!!. Good Drums with crickets and cicada sounds echoing the real insects chirping outside. Trippy short Space literally drips into a very powerful Wharf Rat, one of the best I've heard. Jerrys grizzled voice gives the perfect touch to this song of lost opportunities. -I'll get a new start, live the life I should- They even have some 'fly away' effect during the jam the I havent heard on any other version. This Playin>Drumz>Wharf Rat can hang with any music the boys played in their entire career, no kidding! This is one of my very favorite verisons of Throwing Stones, very guitar and percussion oriented. The whirro(washboard) adds a unique aspect to this version, I've never heard one quite like it. NFA is average for the period(which aint sayin much). The Rain is very sweet, this is probably my favorite of the Beatles songs the boys did.
But again, check this one out for the Playin.

5 stars for the absolutely pristine SBD.
5 for the Playin>Drumz>Wharf Rat.
3 for rest of show.
I sang a little while and then flew on.

Decent show for this late in the band's career. Not sure playing 3 Beatles tunes in one show with the condition of Jerry's voice is a good idea. And any show with Easy Answers and Broken Arrow is not going to be a fav. Great sound quality and PITB.

reviews.reviewbody: if you put good earbuds in Garcias Vocals are decent on Stagger Lee....not saying the recording sucks, the band kinda did this night
I sang a little while and then flew on.

The only show Inwas present for on my birthday. I went on tour alone that summer. These Deer Creek shows were always fun because we could stay at campgrounds. I had my portable dat player with me and would hook up with tapers at the campground after the show to get a copy. I jumped from the lawn into the pavillion right at the start of help>slip. People can say what they want about how the Dead were playing at any point, but live Help>slip on my birthday was possibly the greatest thing in the world at the time and still would be now. Hard to explain how much I loved being on tour.

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

Set 2 HIGHlights: Decent China>Rider. Pretty sure Jerry sunk the Ship of Fools during this intro though. Nearly 20-minute Estimated Prophet. Not mind-blowing, but I will take a massive Estimated from any era. The jam is pretty dynamic throughout, and gets jazzy in the middle with Bobby, Vince, and Jerry blending well. Drums>Space has not been very interesting for me since a few dynamite performances in the spring, but this one is quite nice. Great Wheel>Attics. Fairly good Sugar Mag as well. And they broke out I Fought the Law to acknowledge the gestapo conditions at this show.
12/26/79 including the Caution Jam is maybe 30 seconds longer.

reviews.reviewbody:
Great sound. Thanks for the upgrade CM.

IMHO, a mediocre show (though better than much of 94') highlighted by a truly Grate Terrapin. Recall the "Mock Turtle Jam" from the Cap Center 1990.3.15 show following that Terrapin... This Shoreline 94' performance seems like an extension of those musical ideas. Though supposedly the boys "never played the same show twice" and they probably didn't realize it, these two renditions sound similar. 

First set see's Jerry "sing along" songs and though, "Dont Ease" hadn't been played in well over a year, did we really miss it? 

Playin' Is plain sloppy, with Jer seeming out of the loop. UJB picks up a little steam but is still short of high quality. After Terrapin the show picks up momentum with a solid Drums segment and quality renditions of Stella Blue and Baby Blue. 

So basically we have an above average show for a fairly weak year. IMHO 94' is the weakest year of GD performances next to 92'. This show is dwarfed by the awesome October 1st Boston show just a few weeks later. 

5 Star Sound, REMASTERED MILLER
2 Star performance pre-Terrapin, picks up to steady 3
Total's a 4.

They played Don't ease 6-8-94 and 6-10-94 both in Cal Expo! 6-24-94 Vegas, 7-1-94 Shoreline, pretty much all over the place! Not sure where this stat came from. I had done the entire west coast summer tour in 94 but for this one I was just passing through town on my way to san diego and stopped in to see what was shaking. Skecthy lot scene. Listened out in the lot till West LA and walked back to my car. Sloppy and tired sounding.

Sorry that we couldn't all be born in the "golden age of the dead".  I was grateful for every show i made it to.  My favorite song was well played, "Peggy O".  I always loved Shoreline shows, my first ever show being 6/21/89.  There were highlights in every show, especially if you were there to experience the true flow.  I remember boogeying with a hot little lady up by the wind masts up top during its all over now.....  The drum circle during set break was amazing.....  Bag on us late comers and the band all you want for the last years, It was still the best years of my life....  Anytime i can hear a sbd of a show i was at i will give it a 4.....

reviews.reviewtitle: Fall '94 Shoreline N3: Twenty-Eights Days Between
reviews.reviewbody:
28/41: Samson (7:23) -> Drumz (23:16) -> Days Between (13:02) -> Throwing Stones -> NFA. 

Excellent Miller SBD that really amplifies heavy-metal Weir. Sometimes, tbh, it's jarring, especially contrasted with Garcia's softer, acoustic tone. I have in mind, for example, the Jack-A-Roe and - whoa - Rooster, too. It's perhaps in an effort to compensate for a fading Garcia, though he honestly sounds good, here, on the slide.      Otherwise, the Days Between out of space is chilling as always. So Many Roads is also worth the re-listen. Finally, the second set closing NFA is surprisingly energized- and Brokedown Palace encores.

Jerry is slowing here, but some say this is the best So Many Roads ever? I don't think so, but the weariness in Jerry's voice adds a lot to this song (and Day's Between), and it's closing jam is interesting. My favorite So Many Road is 7/9/95, the last show, but that's probably partly sentimental.

Thank you Charlie! 
This is the last performance of They Love Rach Other by The Grateful Dead.
I sang a little while and then flew on.

UJB->Drumz->Watchtower->SOTM is perhaps worth a visit. Longer, somewhat exploratory Uncle John's segues into a good space - typical for the period - and a sweet and emotional Standing on the Moon. Garcia present for finale.

I find Bobby's guitar sound during this era to be essentially unlistenable.  I meander through Fall '94 looking for those big Jerry moments on SMR or SOTM, but find myself cringing more often than not. Glad to have this, nevertheless!

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

Set 1 Highlights: Lightning Bolt is back, baby! Very good Stranger and TLEO to kick of this multi-night run at the Garden. Unfortunately, it sounds like Bobby went to Guitar Center and bought a $15 digital distortion pedal on the recommendation of a high school kid in a punk-ska-metal band. Pretty ironic that Dan Healy was dismissed for turning Bobby way down in the mixes, and when he is gone, this is what we get. 

Set 2 HIGHlights: China>Rider is quite nice. UJB jam is fairly interesting. SOTM features some excellent "be with you" moments. 

All in all, an okay show, but nothing great. Warming up.

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

Set 1 Highlights: Speedy tempos all around. Unfortunately, most songs feel rushed, and the playing is fairly stock. Things heat up in West LA Fadeaway and El Paso. Decent LRR and Eternity. Vince is on point tonight. 

Set 2 HIGHlights: The setlist may be a bit lackluster, but there are some great things happening here. Victim intro is cool. FOOLISH HEART jam peaks out nicely. Check out that Jam after Samba. The magic kicks in at this point. Very heady Drums>Space and I Need a Miracle is outstanding! Wonderful Black Peter. Great playing from everyone, but Phil just absolutely kills it the rest the show. Great energy into a beautiful Baby Blue. Jerry sings quite well throughout this show.

It's funny how when you live in the moment times lasts forever. This turned out be my swan song with the boys. I felt so proud and relaxed at this venue. Arguably the finest show of 1994. In the near latest period of GD, there are shows like this one that truly stand out.  He came back to echo the final lines af both Stella and So Many Roads. It just goes to show, that even in 94' the nights of brilliance would take place. This entire fall tour was remarkably good considering the end was less than 10 months away.
amazing version of this late era ballad, bravo!!

I spent this evening,"wandering dowtown,with nowhere to go,but just to hang around."I wish now I made more of an effort to score a tix.With Jerry singing with the soul and heart,that he always had,but like at like no other previous night that Fall.The,"So Many Roads,"was one of a kind,it is truely,"timeless!"...By replacing "to EASE,"w/"to HEAL my soul"...He made the song feel,as if He had personal connections to that tune.Without a doubt,He most definetly"walked them roads,"and bless Him,for He just needed someone,"to HEAL His soul."....."SMR"always brings a tear to my eyes,it had personal meaning to me and Jerry.He finally found the one road,to lead Him  home...unforntanetly,I have yet to stumble on that road,but as long as I have Jerry`s music in my heart(and ears!),I`ll keep searching! He now awaits us all,"somewhere beneath the Kokomo" ....and I don`t know about you,but just like Jerry always reminded us,"I WOULD RATHER BE WITH HIM!!".......imissJG,so very,very much.

reviews.reviewbody:
Saw 3 of the fall '94 run... 9/29, 10/1 and 10/3.  Had tickets for the whole run, but life was hectic as a 35 year old attorney and father of 2 young girls.... so I picked and chose based on schedule leaving me with these 3 shows....  other than the train wreck of an I Fought the Law encore on 9/29, I felt like I caught 3 solid shows.... nothing that so much as hinted at the Giants Stadium disaster from August 3rd, or forebode the crash and burn of 1995.....   
 or the train wrecks in DC a week later [4th row center the 3rd night at the US Air Arena fka Cap Center, and Jerry was a mess].... just solid tune selection and playing.... But that's the nature of smack.  A fine line between a euphoric high and being a total waste....   Anyway..... I enjoyed this one.... especially the pre-drumz section of 2nd set..... nice to see Cassidy and GDTRFB in those slots.....   Yes, there were some redeeming moments in 1994.... and as a native of north Jersey and a hater of the Bruins [GO RANGERS!!!], it still rings ironic that the old Boston Garden was the sight of my last good shows......   And my rating is based on a combination of music, song selection, playing, and how much effing fun I had at the show.... and truth be told, the latter bumped it a star!!
reviews.reviewtitle: Boston '94.... my last solidly consistent shows

reviews.reviewbody: I sang a little while and then flew on.

Surprisingly great run of shows. As for this closing night of the Boston run, my highlight is the first set, Bird Song closer. Controlled chaos at its finest. As for the second set, interesting song selection: Box to open, following by Shakedown then Cassidy. Next comes a rare GDTRFB (previously played 29 shows prior, this penultimate version wouldn't be played for another 67 shows, until 7/5/95) that segues into drums. Rare combo - perhaps only a handful of times played - and mostly in '86. I also really like the space and Attics and imagine the Brokedown encore to have been rather emotional.

1994 shows could be hit or miss. This one is a line drive home run! From the first tuneup and opening chords, the band and the crowd seem to recognize that Captain Trips is very much present and accounted for, and the boys take that realization and run with it. Phil has the volume cranked up nicely, and Kreutzmann rattles Touch of Grey into such a frenzy that they actually have to bring it down half a notch for Beat it on Down the Line, which is still a crisp little cooker. The song selection of the first set alone is brilliant, besides the fact that they played it so damn well. It being the closing night of a lengthy stand at the Boston Garden, it seems like they really made an effort to ask themselves "what songs haven't we played yet, and how can we keep this crowd on their toes?" The first set solution: rocker, rocker, rocker, blues standard, ballad, upbeat folk/country tune, ballad, brooding psychedelic jam vehicle. All played to fantastic effect! Bird Song is especially brilliant in a year that saw so many great ones.

A beautiful Box of Rain opens the second set, and they stretch Shakedown way out. Cassidy is marvelous, and GDTRFB, which at the time was a rarity, is peppered with rapid drumming and old school rock & roll guitar licks. Drums > Space really went some places in 1994, and this one saunters away into some murky, aquatic, sonar-like soundscapes before the beacon of Bob Weir's guitar flags it down and lassos it into reach of Garcia's shredding distortion. Bells and robotic birds add to the MIDI madness, and it sounds like it's about to churn into The Other One, but then Lightning Bolt gradually rises from the insanity with a pleasant, unhurried clarity that plucks the band from the depths and places them on The Wheel. Garcia's two American Beauty selections are the real gems of the second set, if not the whole show. From reading the reviews of actual attendees, even though he played brilliantly well this night it seems like a lot of fans and perhaps even Jerry himself knew that this would be his farewell to Massachusetts, making this wonderful post-Space segment even more special.

In a venue that hosted such legendary shows as 4/2/73, 5/7/77, 9/26/91, and 10/1/94, I think the Grateful Dead's final Boston Garden show on 10/3/94 truly has its own special nook in not only the venue's history, but the band's history. This Miller SBD just keeps following me around. I've listened to it all the way through 3 times in the last 5 months and it still amazes me every time. The balance is exquisite and there's a slight echo around the vocals that's almost like a May '77 Betty board. One or two different song selections might've spoiled this show, but the setlist is so beautifully crafted and performed that for me it gets an automatic 5 stars. They can never say Jerry Garcia didn't go out of the Boston Garden with a bang.

reviews.reviewbody:
Great show indeed!
And now, goodbye to the Spectrum, or as some folks called it, the 'Rectum'...because of it's crappy hockey rink sound. However; there's no doubt that we in Philly loved the Grateful Dead, AND that the Grateful Dead loved us right back!
The Spectrum comes down at the end of this month October 2009.

I was lucky enough to score 2nd row seats for this memorable concert.local dj pierre robert intro. the concert and promised a  a good one  and the boys didnt dissapoint. the sugaree was one of the best of the tour and we were treated to a rockin corrina and what sounded like a  matilda jam. also a beautiful version of That would be someting and the dew finished off a stellar show. a must have for your spectrum collection.

I missed the opening with the banner got to the seats just in time for the music to start.  The sound was good and the band was "HOT" the energy was electric and you knew from the start it was going to be a good night. Jerry in shorts!!!! One of my top 5 shows, wish I could go into detail but its been 16 years.  Saw this morning that they brought the old girl down had to find this show "GOD Bless the Grateful Dead"

This is a terrible second set with a phoned in performance.  Set 1 does have some energy but it is all gone by set 2.  Do not waste your time even in the bad era of 1994-95 you can find some gems this show does not really offer any.  If I had to say best songs of Night it would be the Stranger and thats it really. Having relistened the first set is solid set two is terrible, easily among the worst set 2 ever played with Jerry.
I sang a little while and then flew on.

This was the 50th Show at the Spectrum and they raised a banner beforehand to recognize that. I went to this show and remember liking the first set but having to keep myself awake during the 2nd. Anytime Victim is the highlight of the Pre-Drums you know its not boding well. Samba and Corrina had become the kiss of death to 2nd sets by this point and further listening has not swayed that opinion. Morning Dew was nice to close but didn't match the 03-27 version from earlier that year. The fall 94 run had some highlights but I don't think this would be my first choice.

reviews.reviewbody: Ahhh, the corporate juggernaut finally takes hold.   Gone are the "memorial" stadiums, the Autzens, Meadowlands, the "Garden",etc. It is weird to see corporate names attached to every stadium in the USA after the boom years of the 90's.  Insane and profane.   Gone are the days......

I had a  blast at this run and this first show has many highlights.The first set is upbeat focused and long.Set II has some vocal miscues during HC Sunshine & Ship of Fools, much less, and Jerry's playing is inspiring, as is the band.Samson, Way to go and Saint are all very good. Post drums has the last Comes A Time, which many of us waited for since Atlanta, and Jerry  delivers an inspired and hopeful version with a sweet solo and strong vocals and some great playing by Phil too. The set ends strong and the Rain is the second highlight of the night, maybe the song that represents 1994 the best. We should have a  nicer sounding board of this show, it deserves it.
reviews.reviewtitle: It is just a  state of mind...

reviews.reviewbody: Sound quality is terrific! Broken Arrow was awesome, gave me goose bumps! Didnt mind the encore either, not a huge Beatles fan but that was nice...
5 stars for the last comes a time
Super nice!!

Excellent sound as per usual with Charlie transfers. Good show for this era. I mean it doesn't make me forget about the incredible shows from the older era but God damnit it's still the Grateful Dead.

The sound is excellent from Spoonful until about halfway through Big River, when it takes a real phasey turn and sounds like the 'fake live Benny and the Jets' effect on everything. It really ruins it for me. Some might like it as it does give a live feel. It just washes out the detail too much for me. Frail sounding Jerry but heartfelt performance. Last comes a Time a great little gold tooth.
reviews.reviewtitle: Wonky recording. Phasey after Big River

reviews.reviewbody: Cool show, good song selection. Sound quality here seems to change a few times. I drove down from Pittsburgh after seeing Phish for the 1st time the night before. What a gorgeous autumn drive it was! I've had sbd tapes of this show said to be made from patching into the venue's audio system, but I don't know. This was a pretty solid show, I think my 3rd of 3 HSF's and it was a good one. Jerry sounds a little tired on Terrapin, but a good jam ensues. Space was pretty nice, Phil goes off for a while! Post-Drumz was strong too. After the show, some guy in the lot got in an empty golf cart & crashed right into a crowd of people like 10 feet away! This was one of the few venues where I witnessed the police mounted on horses, like dozens of them here & there. Crazy. Anyway, caught a few zzz's at a rest stop going home & woke to another beautiful, frost covered autumn wonderland. See you in'95, Boyz.

reviews.reviewbody:
but a opener is interesting.... 

not complaining

Still remember Jerry shaking off Bobby when Bobby wanted to start the next verse of Women are Smarter. At the time it looked and felt like Jerry had actually caught a decent groove, and he just didn't want to let it go.  As for the rest of the show, the first set is better played than I remembered. A bizarre mix of weak Bobby tunes [Picasso Moon. Easy Answers], Phil's new entry [If the Shoe Fits], the always peppy All Over Now, and Jerry hitting all cylinders on  three favorites [Jack-A-Row, High Time, and Deal].    But for the most part, decently played.  Even Picasso Moon is fast paced and Jerry is well up in the mix.  Second set had its moments.   Jerry had a few spots in Eyes where he was in sync.  But all in all, it was a long and weak version.  As mentioned, Jerry was into Women are Smarter, and it was a decent version of a tune I could usually have lived without.  Samba was Samba.  A decent tune if the first set didn't have Easy Answers and If the Shoe Fits.  He's Gone is a long time favorite [since high school in the early to mid-70's - - class of '76 even if I had zero high school spirit!!].  Jerry stayed on stage for drums and noodled.  Nothing special, but it was obvious he wanted to be playing.   China Doll is yet another long time fav.  Always dripping with emotion.  Sugar Mag was okay.  Thought the version in Boston a week or so earlier blew it away.  Then again, that whole show blew this one away.  Though both had week encores.  Which leads me to Lucy in the Sky With Diamonds..   Absolute train wreck.  Would have preferred the always weak and cheesy I Fought the Law from the Boston show.  What's weird is that was the only sign of melt down all night.  Anyway.....  Had a blast with college buddies.  4th row center.  Nothing like the disaster that was summer '95.  But still a mediocre show at best.  Three stars for Jerry being engaged enough to counter balance some bad Bobby tunes, the requisite Vince tune, If the Shoe Fits, and the train wreck LSD.
I sang a little while and then flew on.
I randomly googled 101194 during an episode and this showed up and it's actually pretty good

Beautiful and last China Doll. Great memories for this show, I camped out for these 3 nights,  managed to get floor seats for the first and third  night middle show seats weren’t bad at f I remember correctly. 94 the year I graduated high school. Great memories of these shows the first night a Rex benefit show, it was fun and I got to see the last Comes A Time. I had fun. I was stone cold sober. Thank you Jerry for the great memories.

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

Last night of this run. Not sure what to think of the USAir Area shows overall. It could just be the recording quality available for these nights (not good), or the fact that Jer seems to stumble a bit with timing issues (his vocals were outstanding all three nights, however), but I would say skip this and move onto MSG. Great setlists, but no major highlights. 

Set 1 Highlights: Party-powder version of Picasso Moon. Pretty peppy version of All Over Now.

Set 2 HIGHlights: 21-minute Eyes. Women are Smarter. Decent He's Gone>Drums>Space>Last "China Doll."

reviews.reviewbody: I Love You Charlie Miller!!!!!

Nice show.  I have really been enjoying 1994 recently despite thinking it wasn't all that at the time.  20/20 hind site, I guess ;)  I have always been a fan of Playin' (the opening riff always seemed like the quintessential Dead "sound" for me) and I tend to favor versions from the 90's.  There is something about the Dead's later sound that just works with it.  I also have to say that never being a huge Vince fan, I have to give the man his props (RIP, Vince).  His playing at this show is great.

one of the best shows of the Vince era. The vocals and intruments are all clear here, and the jamming parts all live up to the band's legend. Yes there are gems to be found in the Vince era, but you sometimes need to sift a little more to find them.
Good MIDI version
A rare visit to the 90's for me. A few too many mumbled lyrics from Jerry but some ok moments too. Let it Grow and Wharf rat were highlights. Nice Baby Blue closer.

Good for 94.  They were on, instrumentally.

But Jerry's singing was off.

Bob was over-using his distortion and whammy bar.  He was playing effects, not notes.

Foolish Heart should have never been in their repertoire.

But it is not bad.  I enjoyed Mexicali Blues more than usual -- it was a fun jam.

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

Last MSG run, and it's going to be good. When picking the best shows of the year, people often point to shows from these final few runs of '94, especially MSG.   

Set 1 HIGHlights: Wonderful openers. Touch hits hard, and Vince really nails the organ on Wang Dang Doodle. Just listen to Jerry wail on Loser! Mexicali jam gets HOT. Dupree's AND Loose Lucy.

Set 2 HIGHlights: Great Foolish Heart jam and outro. The Other One is a great MIDI experiment. The Wharf Rat goes deep. The entire set is worth a play. Baby Blue encore!

reviews.reviewbody: Stranger cooks. Bertha find Garcia emoting different melodies vocally, searchin for the sound. Good Jack A Roe and El Paso really gets going. This might be the best If the Shoe fits I have heard. Make of that what you will. Bird song finds no intro lick and Jerry repeating the first verse in the second verse. The jam is indicative of the chaotic themes 1994 bird songs would feature in the jammed out section. Samson is a little subdued guitar-wise, but Vince has a really great little organ solo thing going. So Many Roads is 80% there lyrically and 90% musically. The ending isn't over the top like 10-1-94 but it builds nice. Saint is top notch. Terrapin is all right, the outro jam has Jerry discovering some new melodies. Stella doesn't have the huge vocal ending, but he does it on guitar instead. A tight Mags and Sunshine. Brokedown Jerry sings the last verse where verse 2 should be, but makes up for it later and repeats some bits. A very good recording. Thanks Rob Eaton.
I sang a little while and then flew on.

Actually might be my favorite of the run. Just heard the first set, again, on TDIGDH - 25 years later. Unique and fun, well-played first set, with what's actually a rare stand-alone Spoonful (not The Same Thing). Otherwise, the Bird Song highlights the set and as one headyversion reviewer puts it: "Over 15 minutes of spacey goodness...." Definitely dig in to the 23-minute Terrapin in the second set, which includes 10-minutes of that 90s era type-2 coda that I can never get enough of. So Many Roads, too, earlier in the set. 42nd of 55.   Brokedown Palace encores and closes out the storied history of the Grateful Dead at Madison Square Garden. The last minute, in particular, is poignant. Show 52/52. "Bye-bye."

reviews.reviewbody: The previous night was best-of-run, with this show being both better and worse. The lows are pretty cringeworthy - even in person, given that a couple of my friends sold/miracled their next night tix and fled. First Set. Wow, Touch as opener again? The last three times they came to Colo they played a Touch opener (12/12/90, 6/28/91 & 12/3/92). This one has no Jer guitar. He shows up halfway into a trainwreck of a Greatest Story. The next several are average, then Bobby plays acoustic on Me & My Uncle. For Big River, Jer leaves it wide open so the focus can be on Vince. Suddenly things click for Loose Lucy, the best song since the first set the night before. Then, shocker, an ace Cassidy. I made a two-AUD matrix of this that sounds better, and I think if we had a SBD we'd be noting this Cassidy as a best-of-era. You don't have to play well the whole set, you only need to leave 'em happy for the break. Second Set. I don't know many Heads that would be chuffed by this setlist, but there is a bonus song before Drums, so take yr least fave and pretend it's not there, and like a Magic Eye poster the setlist improves. Not sure what Jer is trying to do on Victim. The Bobby part is average but the Jer part is weirdly non-committal. On Samba in the Rain, I'm not convinced everyone is playing the same Dead song. Jer loses the thread on Crazy Fingers - and a couple times the whole band. You might think here comes a Bobby song, things will improve. But for Estimated he does his faux-Muppet shouting. The end jam is okay, steered by Vince and Bobby playing squeak-MIDI. Terrapin has more missed cues and jumped half measures. Space is the set peak. Miracle is another mess; again the final jam is led by Vince. In contrary, Standing on the Moon isn't bad. However Lovelight is bathetic as a set closer, with Bobby vamping in front of the most basic possible version. Liberty is just solid enough to leave 'em a little less discomfited. 1st Set:  C- 2nd Set: D- Overall = 1¼ stars [1 + ¼ for Cassidy] Highlights: Cassidy - best of run SOURCES: The _138023_.mgUM70S has much better clarity, especially the second half of set 2. It's not great, but better ones are still MIA, as are SBDs. It needs pitch correction in the first set of +1% for Touch, and -1% for Uncle>Cassidy. It also has very low levels. The 141191_FOB_Schoeps is better in places, with better low end, but I couldn't hang with all the nearby talking.

metadata.notes:
notes:
- The Aqua Net Saga (these recording won't flake or build up while providing lasting control.)
- By the final two Oakland runs (Dec. '94 and Feb. 95) someone had gotten a massive bug up their ass about FOB taping.  The bust circulated early and often.  It was if as they gave security staff an edict to do nothing else but sweep for tapers. Why?  The band was on life support, and the PA system, at least in the sweet spot, was a shell of its former self. But no matter.  If one was so much as standing still and wearing a hat they were bust fodder.  Or if, heaven  forbid, one was standing next to a pile of back packs then the pack might become subject to a quick search.  In order to come out with recordings of these shows, we resorted to extraordinary measures.

Jeff Zimmer, a buddy of mine who worked in Cuppertino at Apple Computer, had long hair.  Typically very politely pulled back in a pony tail. But he was able to fluff it out, rock star style, such the the Schoeps capsules were invisible inside his mane.  So that's great, but what about the power supply and the deck?  Wearing them would be risky, and a bag adjacent to his leg would be even riskier. So he came up with the concept of cutting holes in the soles of a pair of old high tops.  The cables ran down through his shoes, and he made sure to stand where two blankets came together but with no bag or belongings anywhere near his feet.  The cables ran to the back of the blanket where I ran the deck. 

Even so, there is an attempted bust that's quite audible during Lucy in the Sky.  As I recall, after deciding he was clean, security says, "sorry I thought you were someone else."   - John.

- if you already dl'd this, all you need is s1t09 & your good to go.  Sorry bout that.

  It was patched from (2:20 of Easy Answers till end of Set #1. 
  The Patch source is not in the archive. This is different than Source #10933. It cuts in after Candyman.

* Set #2 sounds different. I had a sticky tab in DAT case with a note KM140.
  So Maybe the patch from the Neumann's or the source is KM140 until bust, Schoeps MK4 till end of show...
  I sure someone knows the answer...Easy Answers!

reviews.reviewbody: Sounds good.  Better than the other source.  Good show too.  Lots of spacey jamming from Birdsong on.

reviews.reviewbody: AHH what a night...1st time we ever got great seats from GDTS and it was FRONT ROW!!!We thought it was in the PHILZONE which would of been great but NO Directly in front of JERRY...WOW..Great 1st setTouch,...Wang Dang...ended with a Great BOX OF RAIN,But when they came out 2nd set my friends thought it was Man Smart with BOBBY on Lead Vocals..But when JERRY came up and sang HEY NOW..HEY NOW..IKO IKO....ILL NEVER FORGET THAT NIGHT.....GRIMEY
..I hate to correct anybody, but The First set of this night ended with Eternity, not Box Of Rain as Grimey states in his review. Box>Iko opened set 2.

Yep, It sure was the second set opener..box that is.
Rosemont St. Pats was a grand time...enjoy!

my 65th show, my 23rd playin'. at least it wasn't my 23rd eternity. 
superb quality! not a bad show.

I was there, and I remember they were handing out little saint patricks day stickers.  the highlights of the show for me were 1st set wang dang doodle (love that tune), and my all time favorite Jerry song The Wheel (2nd set)...WOW, this is one of the best Morning Dews I have heard (for this time period).
reviews.reviewtitle: St. Pattys day at the Rosemont

reviews.reviewbody: When The Second Set started I remember Jerry Looking over at Phil and making a box shape with his hands.My brother looks over at Me and says "Box of Rain's comin'" and it did it's great that my most vivid memory is of my brother. Thanks for talkin mom into lettin me go with you to those Dead Show Leo!

Super WoW!  Jerry is in such fine voice.  Thousand of hours of listening to the GD and I'm not convinced I have heard Jerry sound better.  I think the firing of soundman Dan Healy before the 1994 Tour did wonders!!  Jerry's voice is heavily compressed in 1993 and as a result, took away Jerry's subtle nuances.  

Vince with terrific grand piano sound and also some organ throughout.  Bobby supports with tasteful color and Phil digs deep.

The end of song climax is unlike any sort of music I have ever heard.

Check it out. (Bobby plays a horrible steel-drum/guitar dual-voice guitar sound that is so annoying during The Wheel!)

The Mornin Dew/Rain close turned an average show into a memorable show for me and my cohorts.  Rumors had circulated that the Boys would bust out a St. Stephen for St. Patrick's day but Box was as close we got that day.

I am hoping the first night of this run at Rosemont makes it on to the Archive soon.  The first night was epic -- GDTS gave us our first look at the Dead from the 10th row, center. So kind.

Brick Meister

Another good show from this much maligned year. Solid playing from everybody involved. Jerry has that Lightning bolt acoustic like sound going for much of the show and he's wailing too. Though on Playing I think a more electric tone with greater sustain would have worked better, but what are you gonna do? Vince too plays really well and is finally fully integrated into the Dead's sound ('bout time too);-) Bobby too is playing well and is in good voice. His electric tone makes a really nice contrast to Jerry's more acoustic one. Phil once again is barely audible though, damn it all. That's a problem that seems to plague these early '94 boards, just gotta use a little eq (well a lot really). As for the songs the Dew is fantastic, the Althea, Playing, Iko and UJB and subsequent jam are also excellent. Jerry lays out just at the end of the jam and Vince and Bobby do a really cool build that climaxes and fades nicely into drums. And what a remarkable drums and space. One of the best space segments I've ever heard, outstanding. As far as the set goes there's not a clunker in the bunch. A solid 4 star show for 1994, good sound, good set and good playing.
reviews.reviewtitle: Rocking the Rosemont: solid show from '94

reviews.reviewbody: An epic Morning Dew that is a powerhouse. Great Box and Uncle John's Band too.Rain is awesome! Great sounding board to boot.

There are not to many dead songs I dont Like but Eternity is one of them.It seems to last for an Eternity.Most of you will hate me if I tell you the other two songs I dont like,cuz most Heads love them.This is still a Good show and the sound is pretty good so I will give it a 4 for that and a 4 for performance

Grimey posted, "...But when they came out 2nd set my friends thought it was Man Smart with BOBBY on Lead Vocals..But when JERRY came up and sang HEY NOW..HEY NOW..IKO IKO....ILL NEVER FORGET THAT NIGHT.....GRIMEY"

And that my Grimey friend is what the Grateful Dead really were all about ! Cheers !

Very good show. Nice crispy sound too. Every once in awhile I go back and look at my old reviews to make sure I was fair. I relistened to a show the other day and went back to see if I still feel the same about it. Somebody had posted a review bashing me for giving a '90's show four stars when I had given one from the late '70's three stars. That's like comparing apples and oranges. I rate shows against the same year or era. A big part of my review has to do with sound quality. I mean I might find a show wonderful when somone else doesn't. Thats the way life is. I don't expect everyone to like everything I like. Some people are just closed minded and petty I guess.
Pretty OK for the year.

Not as good as night prior, but still a good show. Better second than first set. Really short first set and don’t like that Eternity closer. Otherwise Althea is OK and Lazy River always pleases. Vince sometimes too high in the mix and at times it sounds like they are playing over each other, particularly I hear it during Mexicali. Whose solo is that? Not entirely sure. Same for UJB in second set. Perhaps it was by design, at this point, who knows? Post-space is excellent, culminating in a fine 93 (or any year) Morning Dew. Itself worth the price of admission. Rain encore.
I sang a little while and then flew on.

reviews.reviewtitle: I am on an amazing journey
reviews.reviewbody:
I am listening to every 1994 show in order, mining for gold. 

This night continues the energy of the previous show, and it may be the best show I've heard thus far on the tour. 

Nice Althea, but very out of tune Bobby on the acoustic numbers. Lazy River Road is quite enjoyable, and Eternity gets hot with Vince driving the jam. The second set is excellent throughout. Loved the Playing>UJB.
